question: Should shared `main`-lane background embedded runs permanently surrender one configured concurrency slot to foreground/manual work when capacity exceeds one?
rationale: This is a deliberate default scheduling and throughput policy rather than a correction to an established documented guarantee; the current priority implementation does not settle whether active background work should be capped below configured main-lane concurrency.

options.title: Adopt the one-slot reserve
options.body: Preserve a foreground admission slot on multi-slot main lanes, then rebase the policy into the current lane controller with current-head regression and runtime proof.

options.title: Keep full main-lane background capacity
options.body: Retain the existing concurrency semantics and rely on priority/aging work for queued fairness without reserving inactive capacity.

recommendation.title: Adopt the one-slot reserve
recommendation.body: Preserve a foreground admission slot on multi-slot main lanes, then rebase the policy into the current lane controller with current-head regression and runtime proof.
